sets.title: Form the Participle
sets.description: Choose the correct present active participle
sets.descriptionRussian: Выберите правильное действительное причастие настоящего времени

items.prompt: Человек, _____ книгу, сидит у окна. (The person reading a book is sitting by the window.)
items.promptEnglish: The person reading a book is sitting by the window.
items.hint: Reading NOW = present active participle. читают -> читающий.
items.explanation: Читающий: present active (from читают, -ющий). Who is reading right now.

items.prompt: Девушка, _____ по телефону, улыбается. (The girl talking on the phone is smiling.)
items.promptEnglish: The girl speaking on the phone is smiling.
items.hint: Speaking NOW (fem) = present active. говорят -> говорящая.
items.explanation: Говорящая: present active (fem). From говорят, remove -т, add -щая.

items.prompt: Студенты, _____ русский язык, работают много. (Students studying Russian work a lot.)
items.hint: Studying NOW (plural) = present active. изучают -> изучающие.

items.prompt: Present active participle of РАБОТАТЬ (to work):
items.promptEnglish: Form the present active participle of работать.

items.prompt: Present active participle of ЛЮБИТЬ (to love):
items.promptEnglish: Form the present active participle of любить.

items.prompt: Present active participle of ПИСАТЬ (to write):
items.promptEnglish: Form the present active participle of писать.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The person reading a newspaper (right now).
minimalPairs.explanation: Читающий: present active (reading right now). Читавший would be past (who was reading).

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The person who was reading a newspaper (earlier).
minimalPairs.explanation: Читавший: past active (who was reading). The reading happened in the past.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Children playing in the park (right now).
minimalPairs.explanation: Играющие: present active (plural). Playing right now.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Children who were playing in the park (earlier).
minimalPairs.explanation: Игравшие: past active (plural). They played earlier, not now.

sets.title: Transform and Translate
sets.description: Convert который clauses to participles and back

translation.hint: Studying = present active. изучают -> изучающий (masc nom).
translation.explanation: Изучающий: present active participle (masc nom). Currently studying.

translation.prompt: Children playing in the yard (plural, nominative)
translation.explanation: Играющие: present active (plural nom). Currently playing.

translation.prompt: A woman working at a hospital (fem, nominative)
translation.explanation: Работающая: present active (fem nom). Currently employed there.

translation.prompt: A person who knows several languages (masc, nominative)
translation.explanation: Знающий: present active (masc nom). Who knows languages.

blanks: Люди, _____ здесь, очень дружелюбные. (People living here are very friendly.)
Машина, _____ слишком быстро, опасна. (A car going too fast is dangerous.)
Человек, _____ эту песню, поёт красиво. (The person singing this song sings beautifully.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Present active participle agreement in gender/number/case
explanations: Живущие: present active (plural nom). People who live here.
Едущая: present active (fem nom). A car that is going.
Поющий: present active (masc nom). A person who is singing.

errorCorrection.hint: Девушка is feminine. Participle must agree: читающая.
errorCorrection.explanation: Gender agreement: девушка (fem) -> читающая (fem), not читающий (masc).

errorCorrection.hint: Present active participles can only be formed from imperfective verbs.
errorCorrection.explanation: Perfective verbs have no present tense, so no present participle. Use imperfective: читающий.

errorCorrection.hint: Дети is plural. Participle must agree: играющие.
errorCorrection.explanation: Number agreement: дети (plural) -> играющие (plural), not играющий (singular).

errorCorrection.hint: Мальчика is accusative (animate masc = gen). Participle must match: читающего.
errorCorrection.explanation: Case agreement: вижу мальчика (acc=gen) -> читающего (acc=gen), not nominative.

sets.title: Mixed Challenge
sets.description: Formation, agreement, and usage mixed together

items.prompt: Я разговаривал с женщиной, _____ в нашем офисе. (I spoke with a woman working in our office.)
items.promptEnglish: I spoke with a woman working in our office.
items.hint: С + instrumental -> с женщиной. Participle agrees: fem instrumental = работающей.
items.explanation: С женщиной (fem instr) -> работающей (fem instr). Participle agrees in case.

items.prompt: In which style are present active participles most common?
items.promptEnglish: Where are these participles typically found?
items.hint: Participles are literary. In speech, Russians prefer который.
items.explanation: Participles belong to written/formal style. In everyday speech, который clauses are preferred.

items.prompt: Present active participle of НЕСТИ (to carry): несут -> ?
items.explanation: Несущий: 1st conjugation, -ущий suffix. Who is carrying (right now).

items.prompt: Present active participle of СЛЫШАТЬ (to hear): слышат -> ?
Мы помогли людям, _____ помощи. (We helped people asking for help.)
items.promptEnglish: We helped people who were asking for help.
items.explanation: Помогли людям (dat pl) -> просящим (dat pl). Participle agrees in case and number.

patternRecognition.sentence: читающий / пишущий / работающий (1st conj) vs говорящий / любящий / смотрящий (2nd conj)
patternRecognition.question: What determines whether the suffix is -ущий/-ющий or -ащий/-ящий?
options: Whether the verb is transitive or intransitive
patternRecognition.explanation: The suffix mirrors the 3rd person plural ending: -ут/-ют -> -ущий/-ющий. -ат/-ят -> -ащий/-ящий.

patternRecognition.sentence: Мальчик, читающий книгу. / Мальчика, читающего книгу. / Мальчику, читающему книгу.
patternRecognition.question: What changes in the participle across these three phrases?
options: The case changes to agree with мальчик (nom, acc/gen, dat)
patternRecognition.answer: The case changes to agree with мальчик (nom, acc/gen, dat)
patternRecognition.explanation: Participles decline like adjectives: читающий (nom), читающего (acc=gen), читающему (dat).

blanks: Кошка, _____ на диване, спит. (The cat lying on the couch is sleeping.)
Мы знаем людей, _____ в этом доме. (We know people living in this building.)
explanations: Лежащая: present active (fem nom). The cat lying down.
Живущих: present active (gen/acc pl). People who live there.
